title: Claude Meetings
lede: Anthropic's post introduces Claude Meetings, a beta that brings Claude onto Google Meet calls to answer questions, take notes and build shared docs and whiteboards as the team talks.

points: Claude answers in writing by default and can query connected tools, asking each person's permission the first time.
By default it stays out of calls with outside guests and leaves if one joins; an admin can change that.
It keeps a transcript, summary and screen descriptions, not audio, on a per-meeting page in claude.ai.
During the beta it is unavailable to organisations using zero data retention, HIPAA-ready setups or customer-managed keys.
Notes, transcripts and answers are free in beta, artifacts until February 10, 2027; connected-tool use counts toward plan usage.

points.text: Consent comes up repeatedly, with a joke that objecting to AI recording would simply end up in the notes.
Commenters split on social acceptance; one says vendors already record and transcribe most calls.
Several warn Anthropic keeps moving onto partners' turf, from meeting note takers to integrators building on its models.
Giving meeting agents tool access is called useful but hard to secure, with risks everyday users will struggle to judge.
